Bidding $172 is a clear bargain compared to the $320 list price or $160 mortgage value. The green monopoly premium far exceeds that amount. I will bid this amount and let the other players drop out.

p4 has a dark blue monopoly but only $74 cash. p3 has four houses on Virginia Avenue, yielding $900 in rent. Both players are motivated to block the green set.

Pennsylvania Avenue with four houses yields $1100 in rent. That is far more dangerous than the pink set. I will have only $8 left after paying $172, which is too little for two houses under even-building rules.

Mortgaging Connecticut after winning would give me $608, enough for three houses with $8 left over. Kentucky and Mediterranean together only reach $548. I must bid the full $172 to guarantee the win.

I am currently on Virginia Avenue. I have already passed the pink group this lap. The next time around, I will hit those properties again.

I am checking whether p1's orange monopoly is still active. Indiana is mortgaged, but St James, Tennessee, and New York are all unmortgaged with houses. I need to verify if the mortgage breaks the monopoly and how much rent those properties will collect.

I will bid $171. That is enough to beat p3's cash limit and stop them from raising further.

I will post a short, non-gloating message like "Completing the set."

After winning, I need to build houses quickly. I will mortgage Kentucky and possibly Mediterranean to raise cash. I will not mortgage the greens. I will keep mortgaging Ventnor as a backup for rent hits.

Mortgaging Connecticut after winning at $171 yields $609, enough for three houses with just nine dollars left. That margin is razor thin. One rent hit before building would leave me bankrupt. Three houses on the greens would only collect about $130 each, which is not enough to survive a pink or orange hit.

Two houses on each green would cost $1200. That is too expensive. Three houses is the minimum viable step. Mortgaging Ventnor would raise cash to about $709. That leaves a $109 buffer after building three houses. Ventnor is not in a set. It is unowned. The pink group can charge $700 in rent. I am weighing whether to mortgage it despite my usual rule.

The green monopoly is now the primary win condition. Ventnor can be mortgaged for cash or survival. Three houses on each green cost $600, which is the first viable tier because four houses on one property are not allowed without even building. One house each yields only about $130 in rent, so opponents may not land there. The bank has ten houses remaining, and p3 already owns twelve, p1 seven, and p4 three. I need nine or twelve houses to reach four per property.

The bank has only ten houses available, so I cannot build four on every green. I will build three houses on each property and one extra on Pennsylvania Avenue for a 4-3-3 split. That yields $1100 in rent from PA and $900 from the others. After winning the auction, I will mortgage non-green properties to fund this maximum even-building plan.

I will post a calm, short message like "$171" or "Mine." to signal the bid without revealing my cash strategy. I am also verifying whether p3 actually owns four houses on the pink group, since their recent actions suggest they may have built them.

p1 is currently on Kentucky Avenue with only $15 cash. That property has no houses and no red monopoly, so rent is only $18. They cannot pay that amount. I am checking whether they already paid rent this turn or if they will go bankrupt to me.
